hero.title: A team of AI agents that studies a stock, argues about it, and proposes a trade.
hero.text: During the trading day, AI agents look at a stock's chart, news and finances, debate whether to buy it, and then either propose one specific trade or pass. Ordinary code does all the math and enforces the risk limits, and a person approves every order. It trades with paper (practice) money only.

facts.title: Practice money only
facts.text: Orders go to a paper (simulated) brokerage account. No real money is at risk.

facts.title: AI chooses, code calculates
facts.text: The AI picks from plans that code has already worked out. It never writes a price or decides how many shares to buy.

facts.title: A person approves every trade
facts.text: Nothing is sent until someone types yes.

facts.title: Buy or pass, nothing else
facts.text: It only buys a stock or passes. It never short-sells.

steps.title: Scan
steps.text: Every few minutes, check the watchlist for stocks gapping up on volume with a tight spread and a fresh quote, ranked by relative volume.

steps.title: Event check
steps.text: Before any AI time is spent, skip a stock that isn't proven to report earnings (no SEC 8-K item 2.02 in the last 100 days). The earnings and halt check itself runs at the order ticket and again at approval, and only CLEAR can trade.

steps.title: Analysts
steps.text: Three AI analysts each look at one thing: the price chart, the news, and the company's finances.

steps.title: Plans
steps.text: For each trade setup, code works out the entry price, the stop-loss (where to get out if it goes wrong) and the target.

steps.title: Debate
steps.text: A Bull agent argues for buying and a Bear agent argues against. A fatal objection from the Bear forces a pass.

steps.title: Trader
steps.text: The Trader reads everything, then picks one plan to BUY or decides to PASS.

steps.title: Order ticket
steps.text: Code sizes the order so the worst-case loss stays within the limits, then checks every risk limit and the earnings and halt check. Any failure blocks the order.

steps.title: Approve and log
steps.text: A person approves the ticket in the terminal. Every decision, including passes and skips, is written to the journal.

screens.title: Live run
screens.text: What's happening right now: today's limits, the stocks found, the one being decided and any open position.

screens.title: Decision detail
screens.text: One decision from start to finish: what each agent said and why, the plans, and the order ticket. Open any decision from History.

screens.title: History
screens.text: Every past decision, with filters, and later the results compared with simple strategies.

glossary.text: The Trader's only two answers: propose buying one plan, or don't trade.
The event check stopped the stock before any AI looked at it.
Trading with simulated money in a real brokerage's practice account.
A price below the entry where the position is sold automatically to cap the loss.
A price above the entry where the position is sold automatically to take the profit.
Reward compared with risk. 2R means the target would earn twice what the stop would lose.
What the trade loses if it fills at the limit price and the stop fills at its price. Code keeps it within the per-trade loss limit; a gap through the stop can lose more.
The day's average price, weighted by volume. Price above it is a sign of strength.
Opening-range breakout: price climbing above its high from the first minutes of the day.
Average true range: how much the price typically moves per bar. Used to judge whether a stop is too wide or an entry too far.
The price has already run too far above VWAP, so buying now would be chasing.
How far the stock opened above or below the previous close.
Today's volume compared with normal. Above 1 means more trading than usual.
The gap between the price buyers bid and the price sellers ask. Tight is better.
CLEAR means no earnings or halt nearby. EVENT means there is one. UNKNOWN means the data couldn't confirm. Only CLEAR can trade.
The SEC filing a company uses to report earnings. It's used to confirm the earnings calendar covers the stock.
A Bear argument serious enough that the Trader must pass.
The unit AI usage is measured in. The project has a hard daily cap, shown under Safety limits.
One buy order sent together with its stop-loss and target, so the exits are in place from the start.
The permanent log of every decision and order, which is what these screens read.
